chicken breast.name: Chicken Breast
recommendations: Excellent source of lean protein for muscle building.
Very low in fat; keep portion sizes in check for weight control.
Pair with fresh steamed vegetables for a complete balanced meal.

chicken leg.name: Chicken Leg
recommendations: Good protein source, slightly higher in fat than chicken breast.
Moderate in saturated fats. Enjoy roasted or baked.
Remove skin before eating to decrease overall fat content.

grilled chicken.name: Grilled Chicken
recommendations: Excellent high-protein meal suitable for muscle growth and weight management.
Very low carb and low fat content.
Pair with a side salad to add micronutrients and fiber.

tandoori chicken.name: Tandoori Chicken
recommendations: Flavourful high-protein food marinated in yogurt and spices.
Baking in tandoor keeps the added oils to a minimum.
A great option for lean cutting diets.

chicken curry.name: Chicken Curry
recommendations: Moderate in protein with rich Indian curry spices.
Watch portion sizes due to the oil and cream in gravies.
Pair with roti rather than butter naan to save calories.

egg.name: Boiled Egg
recommendations: Excellent whole protein profile containing healthy fats.
Loaded with vitamins D, B12, and healthy choline.
Good for breakfast or post-workout recovery.

egg white.name: Egg White
recommendations: Pure source of high-quality protein with zero fat.
Excellent for strict low-calorie high-protein diets.
Season with fresh herbs and pepper for flavor.

omelette.name: Omelette
recommendations: Healthy breakfast dish rich in proteins.
Limit oil/butter during pan frying to reduce fats.
Add vegetables (onions, capsicum, spinach) to increase fiber.

fish.name: White Fish Fillet
recommendations: Highly digestible lean protein source.
Low in calories and very low in saturated fats.
Steam, bake, or grill rather than batter-fry.

salmon.name: Salmon Fillet
recommendations: Excellent source of heart-healthy Omega-3 fatty acids.
Promotes joint health, cognitive function, and muscle recovery.
Rich in high-quality proteins.

tuna.name: Canned Tuna in Water
recommendations: Convenient, high-protein lean food.
Extremely low fat, perfect for lean phase diets.
Rinse canned tuna to lower sodium content.

prawns.name: Prawns / Shrimp
recommendations: Very low-calorie food packed with protein and selenium.
Avoid creamy garlic butter sauces to keep fat counts low.
Great choice for lean salads and stir-fries.

paneer.name: Paneer (Cottage Cheese)
recommendations: Rich in calcium and casein protein for vegetarian diets.
Slightly calorie-dense due to fat content. Watch portions.
Opt for low-fat paneer varieties if counting calories.

tofu.name: Firm Tofu
recommendations: Excellent plant-based protein source containing all essential amino acids.
Low in calories and high in calcium.
Highly versatile for healthy vegan stir-fries.

soy chunks.name: Soy Chunks (Soya)
recommendations: Massive protein content (52g per 100g dry).
Loaded with dietary fiber and completely fat-free.
Soak and squeeze out water thoroughly before cooking.

lentils.name: Cooked Lentils (Dal)
recommendations: Excellent plant-based protein and dietary fiber source.
Promotes gut health and matches well with rice or grains.
Very low fat and low glycemic index carb source.

chickpeas.name: Chickpeas (Garbanzo Beans)
recommendations: Provides sustained slow-release energy from complex carbs.
High in soluble fiber, helping to control blood sugar.
Great for healthy salads, hummus, or Indian curry.

kidney beans.name: Kidney Beans (Rajma)
recommendations: High in proteins, potassium, and complex dietary fibers.
Pairs wonderfully with rice to create a complete protein amino profile.
Helps maintain weight management and heart safety.

dal tadka.name: Dal Tadka
recommendations: Healthy lentil soup cooked with turmeric and tempered with cumin spices.
Ghee/oil tempering adds fats; consume mindfully.
High in fiber and vegetarian proteins.

dal fry.name: Dal Fry
recommendations: Comforting Indian lentil dish slightly higher in fats due to pan frying.
Provides steady carbs and gut-friendly fiber.
Limit oil toppings for weight loss goals.

rajma.name: Rajma Masala (Kidney Bean Gravy)
recommendations: Comforting kidney bean curry loaded with plant protein.
Excellent source of iron, potassium, and fiber.
Highly recommended for heart health and clean energy.

chole.name: Chole Masala (Chickpea Curry)
recommendations: Spicy Indian chickpea gravy providing dense complex carbohydrates.
Watch the portion sizes as the gravy is oil-based.
Serve with whole-wheat roti or plain rice rather than deep-fried bhature.

biryani.name: Chicken Biryani
recommendations: Aromatic, spiced rice dish containing high-quality proteins.
Calorie-dense; manage portion sizes carefully.
Pair with a side raita (yogurt dip) to balance digestion.

pulao.name: Vegetable Pulao
recommendations: Mildly spiced basmati rice dish with loaded vegetables.
Excellent quick energy source.
Substitute white rice with brown rice for a higher fiber count.

jeera rice.name: Jeera Rice
recommendations: Basmati rice flavored with ghee and cumin seeds.
Cumin seeds aid digestion.
Slightly higher calories than plain rice due to tempering fats.

plain rice.name: Steamed White Rice
recommendations: Clean source of easily digestible carbohydrates.
Virtually fat-free; excellent for energy loading.
Pair with rich protein dals and legumes.

roti.name: Whole Wheat Roti
recommendations: Outstanding staple carb containing high dietary fiber.
Low fat when cooked dry without ghee oil brush.
Highly recommended for active energy days.

naan.name: Butter Naan
recommendations: Refined flour flatbread brushed with butter.
High in simple carbohydrates and fats. Limit consumption.
Pair with high protein curries.

paratha.name: Plain Laccha Paratha
recommendations: Layered Indian flatbread cooked with oil or ghee.
Higher in calories than roti due to pan frying.
Good for active days but moderate your portion sizes.

aloo paratha.name: Aloo Paratha
recommendations: Potato-stuffed flatbread. Heavy carb-dense meal.
Usually served with butter or pickle which adds sodium and fat.
Good for pre-workout energy, watch portion sizes.

paneer butter masala.name: Paneer Butter Masala
recommendations: Rich paneer dish cooked in butter and cream tomato gravy.
Excellent calcium source but very high in fats and calories.
Manage portion sizes strictly.

butter chicken.name: Butter Chicken
recommendations: Indian classic containing grilled chicken in a creamy butter sauce.
High in proteins but also high in saturated fats and sodium.
Reserve as an occasional treat.

palak paneer.name: Palak Paneer
recommendations: Healthy paneer cubes cooked in a spinach puree gravy.
Rich in iron, vitamins, calcium, and dietary protein.
Considered one of the healthiest vegetarian Indian dishes.

dosa.name: Masala Dosa
recommendations: Crispy fermented rice-lentil crepe stuffed with potato masala.
Contains gut-friendly probiotics from fermentation.
Limit oil brushing to make it healthier.

idli.name: Steamed Idli
recommendations: Steamed rice-lentil cakes, extremely low in fat.
Easily digestible, gut-friendly breakfast choice.
Serve with healthy lentil sambar.

sambar.name: Sambar
recommendations: Vegetable-lentil broth, high in vitamins and fiber.
Low in calories, perfect companion for idli or dosa.
Watch sodium levels.

poha.name: Poha
recommendations: Flattened rice flakes cooked with spices, onions, and peanuts.
Light breakfast option supplying clean carbohydrates.
Peanuts add healthy proteins and fats.

upma.name: Upma
recommendations: Semolina porridge cooked with mild spices and vegetables.
Good quick source of energy.
Add carrots and peas to increase nutritional value.

vada pav.name: Vada Pav
recommendations: Mumbai street burger with a deep-fried potato dumpling in bread.
High in carbs, fat, and sodium. Fast energy, but poor satiety.
Eat occasionally as a cheat meal.

pav bhaji.name: Pav Bhaji
recommendations: Mashed vegetable curry served with toasted butter buns.
Bhaji has good vegetable density, but butter on Pav increases fat.
Try wheat buns toasted with minimal butter to cut fats.

burger.name: Chicken Burger
recommendations: Moderate protein source; check mayo and sauce layers.
High in sodium and refined flour carbs.
Swap side fries for water or salads.

cheeseburger.name: Classic Cheeseburger
recommendations: Excellent protein source, but high in cholesterol and sodium.
Calorie-dense; manage portion sizes carefully.
Swap side fries for salads or water.

pizza.name: Cheese Pizza
recommendations: High in saturated fats and sodium; consume in moderation.
Include a side salad to increase dietary fiber intake.
Opt for thin crust and load up on veggies to lower calories.

pasta.name: Vegetable Pasta
recommendations: Good source of energy from carbohydrates.
Load up on vegetables like zucchini and tomatoes to add fiber and vitamins.
Use olive oil sparingly to keep fat counts low.

spaghetti.name: Spaghetti Bolognese
recommendations: Rich source of protein and complex carbohydrates.
Opt for whole wheat pasta to double the fiber content.
Top with fresh basil and minimal cheese.

french fries.name: Golden French Fries
recommendations: Deep-fried; high in processed fats and sodium.
Low satiety despite high calories.
Enjoy occasionally, choose baked potato wedges if possible.

hot dog.name: Classic Hot Dog
recommendations: Processed meat high in sodium and saturated fats.
Low nutrient density.
Eat occasionally; garnish with mustard rather than mayo.

sandwich.name: Veggie Club Sandwich
recommendations: Moderate proteins; good mid-day meal option.
Choose multi-grain bread to increase dietary fiber.
Limit high-calorie sauces and mayonnaise.

shawarma.name: Chicken Shawarma Wrap
recommendations: High-protein street food wrap.
Mayonnaise and garlic sauces add significant fats.
Opt for whole-wheat wrap and loaded salad vegetables.

wrap.name: Grilled Chicken Wrap
recommendations: Excellent balanced meal option.
Rich in proteins and low in saturated fats compared to burgers.
Choose low-fat dressings.

taco.name: Beef Taco
recommendations: Tasty protein-carb balance.
Toppings like cheese and sour cream increase fats.
Load up on pico de gallo and lettuce.

burrito.name: Chicken Burrito
recommendations: Very filling meal containing beans, rice, and proteins.
Can be calorie-dense; watch wrap size.
Swap white rice with brown rice or black beans for better fiber.

fried chicken.name: Crispy Fried Chicken
recommendations: Deep-fried and breaded. Very high in fats and sodium.
Good protein source, but outweighed by the calorie density.
Remove batter coating if eating to cut down on oils.

apple.name: Fresh Apple
recommendations: Highly nutritional fruit loaded with antioxidants.
Contains soluble fiber pectin that aids cholesterol control.
Excellent low-calorie snack for curbing sugar cravings.

banana.name: Fresh Banana
recommendations: Outstanding source of potassium and instant carb energy.
Perfect pre- or post-workout quick snack.
Helps regulate muscle cramps and heartbeat.

mango.name: Ripe Mango
recommendations: Delicious tropical fruit high in vitamin A and C.
Slightly higher sugar density than berries; manage portions.
Excellent raw or in morning smoothies.

orange.name: Orange
recommendations: Superb source of Vitamin C and hydration.
Contains dietary fiber which helps digestion.
Prefer whole fruit over juicing to retain fibers.

pineapple.name: Pineapple
recommendations: Contains bromelain, a digestive enzyme that breaks down proteins.
Boasts anti-inflammatory properties.
High in vitamin C.

watermelon.name: Watermelon
recommendations: Extremely hydrating (92% water) and very low calorie.
Contains lycopene, a powerful antioxidant.
Great for hot summer days and post-workout rehydration.

grapes.name: Grapes
recommendations: High in resveratrol, which supports cardiovascular safety.
Relatively high sugar concentration; eat in moderation.
Excellent cold snack choice.

strawberry.name: Strawberry
recommendations: Extremely low calorie and packed with antioxidants.
Great choice for satisfying a sweet tooth on cutting diets.
Very high in Vitamin C.

kiwi.name: Kiwi Fruit
recommendations: Very high concentration of Vitamin C and Vitamin K.
Dietary fiber supports regular digestion.
Contains actinidain, a protein-dissolving enzyme.

papaya.name: Fresh Papaya
recommendations: Contains papain, which eases gastrointestinal digestion.
Rich in beta-carotene and vitamin C.
Outstanding low-calorie fruit choice.

guava.name: Fresh Guava
recommendations: Incredibly high in fiber (5.4g per 100g).
Contains more Vitamin C than oranges.
Maintains excellent blood pressure control.

potato.name: Boiled Potato
recommendations: High in potassium and complex carbohydrates.
Extremely high satiety index.
Eat skin to retain optimal fiber; avoid frying.

tomato.name: Red Tomato
recommendations: Extremely low calorie; excellent source of lycopene.
Supports skin health and cellular protection.
Great base for healthy low-fat gravies.

onion.name: Onion
recommendations: Contains prebiotic fibers that nourish gut bacteria.
Rich in organosulfur compounds.
Adds rich flavor to cooking without adding fats.

carrot.name: Orange Carrot
recommendations: Outstanding source of beta-carotene (Vitamin A).
Promotes eye safety and cellular repair.
Low-calorie sweet crunching snack.

broccoli.name: Broccoli
recommendations: Contains sulforaphane, a powerful compound.
Rich in calcium, fiber, and Vitamin C.
Highly recommended food for fat loss and detox.

cabbage.name: Green Cabbage
recommendations: Very low calorie density; aids in stomach lining protection.
High in vitamin K and vitamin C.
Great volume food for volume eating.

spinach.name: Fresh Spinach
recommendations: Extremely nutrient dense; high in iron, lutein, and calcium.
Low in calories, promotes cardiovascular health.
Avoid boiling to retain water-soluble nutrients.

cauliflower.name: Cauliflower
recommendations: Low-carb substitute for grains (e.g. cauliflower rice).
Contains choline, which supports brain health.
Rich in vitamins C and K.

capsicum.name: Bell Pepper (Capsicum)
recommendations: Excellent vitamin C source.
Low calorie and highly hydrating.
Adds rich texture and color to healthy meals.

peas.name: Green Peas
recommendations: Relatively high protein count compared to other vegetables.
High in fiber; promotes stable blood glucose.
Pairs well with rice and curries.

gulab jamun.name: Gulab Jamun
recommendations: Deep fried dough balls soaked in high sugar syrup.
Extremely high in simple sugars and saturated fats. Limit strictly.
Triggers quick insulin spikes.

rasgulla.name: Rasgulla
recommendations: Indian cheese sweet soaked in sugar syrup.
Lower in fat than gulab jamun but still very high in sugars.
Squeeze out syrup before eating to lower calorie intake.

ice cream.name: Vanilla Ice Cream
recommendations: High in sugar and dairy cream fats.
Provides quick energy but low satiety.
Try frozen yogurt or fruit sorbet alternatives.

brownie.name: Chocolate Brownie
recommendations: Very high in refined sugars and baking butter fats.
Highly calorie-dense; consume in moderation.
Serve with fresh berries to add fiber.

cake.name: Chocolate Fudge Cake
recommendations: High simple carbs and butter fat load.
Triggers rapid blood sugar spike.
Enjoy occasionally for celebrations.

donut.name: Glazed Donut
recommendations: Deep fried refined dough glazed in sugar.
High in trans/saturated fats and simple sugars.
Limit consumption strictly.

chocolate.name: Milk Chocolate Bar
recommendations: Highly calorie dense; high sugars and dairy fats.
Satisfies quick cravings, but has low volume satiety.
Prefer 75%+ dark chocolate for antioxidant benefits.

cookies.name: Chocolate Chip Cookies
recommendations: High in refined baking butter and sugars.
High calorie to weight ratio.
Drink with water or skim milk.

tea.name: Chai (Milk Tea with Sugar)
recommendations: Comforting daily beverage, contains antioxidants from tea leaves.
Added sugar and whole milk add simple calories.
Substitute sugar with stevia and use skim milk to cut calories.

coffee.name: Cappuccino (Whole Milk, No Sugar)
recommendations: Provides moderate caffeine boost to improve metabolism.
Avoid adding syrups and sugars to preserve weight loss properties.
Opt for almond/skim milk options.

milk.name: Whole Milk
recommendations: Excellent source of calcium, vitamin D, and proteins.
Contains saturated dairy fats.
Consider skimmed or low-fat varieties to save calories.

lassi.name: Sweet Lassi
recommendations: Traditional Indian yogurt drink; contains gut-friendly probiotics.
High in simple sugars from flavorings; drink in moderation.
Choose salted or spice-tempered chaas (buttermilk) to save calories.

coke.name: Coca-Cola Classic
recommendations: Zero nutritional value; high in simple refined high-fructose sugars.
Causes rapid insulin spikes. Leads to fat accumulation.
Prefer Diet/Zero version or sparkling water.

pepsi.name: Pepsi Cola
recommendations: High in liquid sugar calories; zero satiety index.
Causes rapid glucose spikes and teeth decay.
Prefer zero sugar alternatives.

juice.name: Fresh Orange Juice
recommendations: Provides vitamin C, but lacks the beneficial fibers of whole oranges.
Allows fast sugar absorption. Keep portions small.
Prefer eating whole fruits to maintain proper satiety.

smoothie.name: Banana Strawberry Smoothie
recommendations: Filling and packed with fruit vitamins and dietary fibers.
Watch high-calorie additions like peanut butter, honey, or protein powders.
Great choice for post-workout nutrition.
